summary: Missoula County Sheep Mountain lookout, about 10 miles NE of Missoula: L-4 cab, staffed in 1934, listed gone; a 1966 item conflicts with the gone-by-1962 date.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone and firelookout.com says gone by 1962, but a 1966 newspaper item describes the lookout as staffed

events.note: newspaper mentions a forest lookout station on Sheep Mountain east of Missoula
Daily Missoulian reports a new lookout to be built on the peak that summer
firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1933; newspaper dates differ
Carl Rooney sent to the lookout in May; Ralph Hogan named lookout in July
source gives only the decade: Abandoned 1940s
listed as gone by 1962; the source does not say how
newspaper item names J. Penkake as assigned to the lookout north of Missoula; conflicts with the 1940s and 1962 dates

evidence.supports: L-4 cabin dated 1933; abandoned in the 1940s; gone by 1962
April 1930 report of a new lookout to be built that summer, back of Jumbo
evidence.quote: Among the improvement projects of the Missoula forest this summer will be a new lookout to be constructed on Sheep mountain, back of Jumbo, covering the drainages in that vicinity.

evidence.supports: 1925 forest lookout station on Sheep Mountain east of Missoula
evidence.quote: Two inches of snow fell Sunday on Sheep mountain east of here up the Blackfoot valley, according to a report from the forest lookout station there.

evidence.supports: Carl Rooney sent to the lookout in May 1934
evidence.quote: Carl Rooney was sent to the Sheep Mountain lookout.

evidence.supports: Ralph Hogan was the lookout in July 1934
evidence.quote: Ralph Hogan is lookout on Sheep Mountain, north and east of Missoula.

evidence.supports: 1966 item: J. Penkake assigned to the lookout north of Missoula
evidence.quote: Airmail service for the Sheep Mountain lookout is reported by J. Penkake, assigned to that elevated point north of Missoula.

evidence.supports: Missoula County Sheep Mountain listed as gone
the Mineral County entry covers a different peak
a cabin built in 1928 on a Sheep Mountain 15 miles southwest of Superior
evidence.quote: has been constructed by C.P. Fickes and J.B. Halm on Sheep mountain, 15 miles southwest of Superior.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two Sheep Mountains appear in these sources. The Mineral County peak near Superior, with its 1928 cabin, is a different site and is kept out of this record.

notes_for_editor: Build date is unsettled: a 1925 station mention, a 1930 newspaper plan for a new lookout that summer, and firelookout.com's 1933 date. The 1966 item conflicts with firelookout.com's abandoned-1940s and gone-by-1962 dates; I could not resolve it and it may describe a different structure. The FFLA list also has a second Sheep Mountain tagged Missoula at 47.18064, -115.05476 (Ground, Gone); it is probably the Mineral County area and I did not check it. Mineral County history (mtmemory.org node 128382 and the 1928 newspaper items) belongs to a different site and should not be merged here. No source I read describes what remains on the peak today or whether it is open to the public.
